newsitem.title: JAPAN: Lending to Japan contractors falls in 95/96 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Lending to Japan contractors falls in 95/96 - survey.

text.p: Outstanding lending by Japanese banks to the nation's construction sector fell 500 billion yen from a year earlier to 30.85 trillion yen at the end of the 1995/96 business year, a research firm said.
Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co said it was the first year-on-year decline since it began such surveys in 1990.

The decline in the balance of lending by Japan's 145 banks at the end of last March reflected their cautious stance on providing loans to construction companies, which have been suffering from slow economic recovery and falling land prices, it said in a report.

At the end of March 1991, loans outstanding by the banks to the construction sector totalled 24.64 trillion yen. The figure gradually rose to a high of 31.35 trillion yen at the end of March 1995, it said.
Analysts said unrealised losses on real estate holdings of Japanese general contractors were growing due to the five-year slump in the real estate market.

In addition, Japan's general contractors as a whole are estimated to have more than three trillion yen worth of liabilities as a result of guarantees they gave on bank loans made to developers, they said.
